title: Network CSV rerun coordinator batch start
summary: Added the confirmed coordinator-owned Network CSV rerun batch start path without worker execution.
reason: Network CSV rerun needs durable coordinator batch state and command journal evidence before later phases can enable row claims.
behavior_before: Network CSV rerun had a read-only preview and no-write start dry-run, but no confirmed route could create durable coordinator-owned network CSV rerun batch state or strict command journal evidence.
behavior_after: POST /api/rerun/network/start requires a matching backend dry-run fingerprint and confirm_start=true, writes exactly one desktop_rerun_network_batch.v1 file under State/Rerun/Network with rows claim-disabled until Phase 4, records strict command journal evidence, cleans up the state file if strict journal recording fails, and blocks close-readiness while the active batch state exists. The phase still does not start workers, create claims, stage sources, mutate queue state, mutate pending publish, mutate final output, or touch media.
rollback_plan: Remove the /api/rerun/network/start route registrations, strict payload and route-contract entries, start_network_rerun_csv_batch and supporting batch-state helpers, close-readiness batch-state guard, tests, inventory rows, state schema documentation, and refreshed generated summaries. Delete any Phase 3 network-rerun-*.json test artifacts from temporary state roots only; no source media, output media, pending-publish manifests, completed manifests, normal queue state, or worker claims are produced by this phase.
notes:
Phase goal and boundaries: add POST /api/rerun/network/start as a confirmed start path that writes only coordinator-owned network CSV rerun batch state plus command journal evidence; keep rows claim-disabled/not-yet-claimable; do not start workers, stage sources, mutate queue, mutate pending publish, mutate final output, or touch media.
High-risk surfaces: network lifecycle coordinator authority, command journal evidence, duplicate batch guard, strict JSON confirmation, close-readiness while active batch state exists, and state-file schema inventory.
Validation rung: targeted command contract tests, start success/failure command-journal tests, state-file schema inventory coverage, close-readiness active-batch test, stop/cancel dry-run tests if stop/cancel surface is introduced. Real-media validation is not required because this phase does not stage or process media.
Stop/cancel dry-run routes were not introduced in this phase; rows are claim-disabled and no worker claims exist, so cooperative stop-after-current semantics remain a Phase 4+ control-route concern.
